alignments.note: Verb; the explicit pronoun takes the English subject.
Existential particle; the ASV recasts the clause verbally and writes nothing for it.
Preposition left with nothing by the recasting (rule 40).
Comparative preposition absorbed into 'excelleth'; not contiguous with it, so rule 2 splits and it is unrepresented (rules 30, 35).

Comparative preposition rendered by the whole frame 'as far as', which is one rendering rather than one token (rule 30). Head on the opening 'as', the relational word that realizes כְּ's own lexeme (rule 24, first sentence), with the degree adverb 'far' inside the unit: rule 24's degree-word ruling heads a comparative rendered by a degree adverb together with its relational word on the relational word, as מִן -> 'more than' heads on 'than' at ECC.2.9 and כְּ -> 'As ... so' heads on 'As' at ECC.2.15. The competing reading heads on 'far' as the content word the phrase turns on; that sentence of rule 24 reaches only a rendering in which no word realizes the morpheme's lexeme, and here 'as' does. A further competing reading splits the frame across כְּ and the second יִתְרוֹן.
Noun rendered by the finite 'excelleth', as in the first line.

review_notes: 'as far as' is taken whole as the rendering of the comparative כְּ; the competing reading splits it across כְּ and the second יִתְרוֹן.

Reconciliation moved the head of the 'as far as' unit from 'far' to 'as'. Rule 24 heads a comparative preposition on the relational word and leaves the degree adverb inside the unit, which is how this chapter heads מִן -> 'more than' on 'than' at ECC.2.9, כְּ -> 'As ... so' on 'As' at ECC.2.15 and עִם -> 'even as' on 'as' at ECC.2.16. Only the head moved; the unit's edges are unchanged.
